newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Mata field to up output 30-fold in 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Mata field to up output 30-fold in 3 yrs.

text.p: Oil output at Venezuela's Mata field is seen increasing thirty times to 18,000 barrels per day (bpd) in three years following a planned $80 million investment, the consortium that successfully bid for the field on Monday said.

"We expect to produce 18,000 barrels per day (in three years) ... although there are conditions to produce up to 60,000 bpd," Pivensa acting president Antonio Pardo told reporters after the auction. The field currently produces 600 barrels per day from four active wells.

The 50/50 consortium, which groups local mining company PBE Trading and Venezuelan aluminum firm Pivensa, agreed to pay just over $90 million for the field's 20 year operating contract in Venezuela's third round of oil auctions which began Monday and continues through the week.
The surprisingly high bid pipped by three million dollars the second highest $87 million offer by local Corporacion Corepli de Venezuela in association with Argentina's Perez Companc .

"We reckon that proven reserves are worth some $5 billion, using an oil price of $18 per barrel," Pardo explained. State oil company PDVSA has estimated proven reserves at 101 million barrels, but Pardo said the field could have anywhere between 170 and 300 million barrels.
Pardo added the consortium might re-jig its capital structure with local firm Marshall and Assoc. taking a 20 percent share.
